<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getReferences (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getReferences, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/references), meta.getReferences (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/references, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/references))_
- `content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/references (route, bridged from symbol findReferencesToMeta — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via findReferencesToMeta (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4c0b45469a3fe69691124ff611510106e7396397` — the merge of head `8ca891b1d5e9a83ee57b6ed14bf4f67c0e8eeb73` into base `8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4c0b45469a3fe69691124ff611510106e7396397 && git checkout 4c0b45469a3fe69691124ff611510106e7396397
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad 8ca891b1d5e9a83ee57b6ed14bf4f67c0e8eeb73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad && git merge --no-ff 8ca891b1d5e9a83ee57b6ed14bf4f67c0e8eeb73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8226755ee94cd6fe26a1580daea58251e4af99ad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6178702290` (amendment `6179854093`) on #23539 · reviewed head `8ca891b1d5` · 2026-10-14T23:14Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23554`). 5 files, +469 / −12. `Clause-②: no`: the references answer keeps its declared shape and gains the missing row, and no door changes what it accepts. No contract review is owed; this record is the review.

1. **Shape.** Draft PR. The first line is `Fixes #23539`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at line start. The changeset is `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`.
2. **Scope against the amended claim.** Route A, as accepted.
   - `reference-sites.ts` gains a composite-key seed with derived, fail-closed premises: `permission` still declares `fields` as a root record, and `ObjectSchema.name` still rejects `.`. It sits in its own `compositeKeyByTarget` map, never in `byTarget`.
   - `protocol.ts` changes only in the two amended regions:
     - a new `collectCompositeKeyHeadHits` after `collectReferenceHits`, with `referencedNamesAt` and `collectReferenceHits` byte-unchanged;
     - the matcher fold inside `findReferencesToMeta`.
   - `duplicatePackage` has 0 hunks.
3. **The change, read in the diff.**
   - A key names the target only when the text before its FIRST `.` equals the target's name, which is the split `getFieldPermissions` makes.
   - A key with no `.`, or with a `.` at index 0, names nothing.
   - The field part is never read, so `invoice.customer` is not a reference to `customer`.
   - There is one row per site, at path `fields{key}`, with kind `permission fields`.
   - A source type named only by a composite site still gets its matcher, on the same one-read-per-source-type walk.
4. **Evidence.**
   - **The real-kernel pin:** red on `main` (2 failed, 2 passed), green after the fix (4/4), and red again when the walk branch is ablated. The restore is proven blob for blob.
   - **The `field`-target 501** (#9538's ground) is byte-identical before and after, by message hash.
   - **The `duplicatePackage` invariant:** the derivation pin asserts that `byTarget('object')` has no `permission.fields` site, and the `protocol-duplicate-package-*` suites are green.
   - **Full suites:** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 28412 passed / 19 skipped, and `@objectstack/objectql` 8112 passed. Typecheck exit 0.
   - **Local gates:** 67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, prerequisite not met; CI runs it).
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - The empty-object-part FLS key: filed by this seat as #23549 (now p1, claimed by seat 1).
   - The `field`-target refusal's sentence about "bare" field names: an Acceptance note, `carrier:` none.
   - `duplicatePackage` reading `byTarget('object')` as a flat property set: guarded by the new derivation assertion.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) Every check is green or skipped by design: read at landing. 17 runs were in progress at this record.
   - (b) `mergeable_state` is clean at enqueue: read at landing.
